Specify -std=c99 compiler flag for Cython files.

PyTorch's build_ext subclass automatically adds -std=c++14 to everything,
disregarding whether it's a C or C++ file. Clang throws an error with this
flag (gcc only prints a warning).
To work-around PyTorch's behavior we can specify a correct -std flag for

Ensure storage_offset is int

Older versions of PyTorch complain if storage_offset is e.g. a np.int64
object (which it will be in certain cases, since it is the return value
of a np.prod call). We cast to int to make sure this is not a problem.

This should be done for size, stride and probably other arguments as well,
but since it's not a problem on newer PyTorch versions we keep things as
they are, since those are usually not np.int64.

Falkonv7.1

Hyperparameter optimization (falkon_hopt module) and a big refactoring.

The most significant changes are:
 - Consolidated C/CUDA extensions in the csrc directory. This
   helps with compilation time, and package size.
 - Consolidated the fMM, fMMv APIs to avoid having to deal with
   separate CPU, CUDA imlementations. There is still some work
   to do here for the batch APIs.
 - Changed the kernel API to allow for differentiable kernel
   computations. This was necessary to implement the hyperparameter
   optimization module.
 - Added falkon_hopt module for hyperparameter optimization (gradient
   based) with several different objective functions.
 - Some work done on the CI side, but still partial/not working.

Transposes of Q's don't have specialized functions and fall back to `AbstractMatrix` methods, in particular in multiplication. feat(vispy-plotter): implement heuristic to ensure performance

We implement a heuristic based on a `precision` tuple. This takes two
parameters:

- the number of decimals that should be used to group segments into
  meshes
- the total number of meshes to limit the visualization to.

In general, more meshes means more detail, but less performance. Here,
the user can provide what precision they want to use. The method
includes a heuristic where it will reduce precision until the number of
meshes being used is less than the provided threshold value.

fix(file-list): correct recursive file listing

When there are models that follow a recursive structure. For example:

```
something.net.nml -> ./cells/cell.nml -> ./channels/channel.nml
```

When processing the cell.nml file, we must do it relative to its
location, not relative to the root file (something.net.nml) so that the
paths are correct in the final list of files included in the model.

We do this by making sure that when recursing through the list, we pass
the location of the "new" rootfile, and when we append the processed
file to the file list, we include its "rootdir", which would be relevant
to the "main" rootfile.

feat(vispy-3d-detailed): take advantage of lru_cache

We make the function arguments all hashable so that we can use the
lru_cache here also. For most networks, there will be one cell object
that is placed at different locations in the population by specifying an
offset. The mesh creator takes the offset into account, but other than
that, it is not used. So, we don't need to pass it to our cell specific
method. For all cells of the same type for the population, we only
process the first one, and the rest of the meshes are taken from the
cache. We then add the offset for each cell instance to the mesh data
before passing it to the mesh creator.

So, for 100 cells of the same type, we only process the one cell.
The other 99 are picked from the cache.

For the moment, I've set the lru size to 100. I don't think we'll come
across networks that use more than 100 cells anytime soon.

Note that this does not help for cases where the same cell has also been
rotated because for each of these cells, NeuroML requires a new
population. There, we must process each cell individually, for each
population.

Export 2D UNet to DeepImageJ format

Major changes:
- Add an appendix at the end of the notebook to export the trained model to DeepImageJ bundled model format. It creates a new folder called "deepimagej" inside the model folder. "deepimagej" contains all the files needed for its execution/test in Fiji and is compatible with DeepImageJ version 1.0.1, i.e. the configuration file is in XML format.
- The resulting image in DeepImageJ is slightly different. Two are the reasons:
    · DeepImageJ takes into account the halo of the model (receptive field of the pixel).
    · Percentile Normalization: it may vary slightly from ImageJ and Python. See the macro code here: https://github.com/deepimagej/imagej-macros/blob/master/PercentileNormalization.ijm

Minor changes:

feat: Introduce Delaunay Refinement (Ruppert's Algorithm)

Adds support for Delaunay mesh refinement using Ruppert's algorithm.
This feature aims to improve the quality of triangles in a Triangulated
Irregular Network (TIN) by iteratively inserting points.

Key components of this change:

1.  **`RuppertsRefiner.java`** (in `org.tinfour.refinement`):
    *   The main class that orchestrates the refinement process.
    *   It takes an `IIncrementalTin` and quality criteria (minimum angle
        and/or maximum circumradius-to-shortest-edge ratio).
    *   The refinement loop identifies "poor-quality" triangles and
        "encroached" segments (constrained edges whose diametral circles
        are pierced by other TIN vertices or by circumcenters of
        poor-quality triangles).
    *   Poor-quality triangles have their circumcenters inserted, unless
        doing so would encroach a segment; in that case, the segment
        is split.
    *   Encroached segments are split by inserting their midpoints.
    *   The process continues until no poor-quality triangles or
        encroached segments remain according to the criteria.

2.  **Utility Classes** (in `org.tinfour.utils`):
    *   **`TriangleUtility.java`**: Provides helper methods for triangle
        calculations, such as computing angles, finding the shortest
        edge, calculating the circumradius-to-shortest-edge ratio,
        and determining if a triangle meets the quality criteria.
    *   **`SegmentUtility.java`**: Provides helper methods for segment
        (edge) calculations, including computing a segment's
        diametral circle and checking if a point encroaches upon
        a segment.
    *   **`Circle.java`**: A simple class to represent a circle, used
        for diametral circle calculations.

3.  **Testing:**
    *   JUnit tests were added for `TriangleUtility`, `SegmentUtility`,
        `Circle`, and `RuppertsRefiner`.
    *   Tests cover various scenarios, including valid inputs, edge cases,
        degenerate conditions, and the different logic paths within the
        refinement algorithm.

4.  **Documentation:**
    *   Javadoc comments were added to all new public classes, methods,
        and constructors to explain their purpose, parameters, and behavior.

The current implementation of `RuppertsRefiner` uses a straightforward
approach where the queue of items to process is fully refreshed after
each modification to the TIN. While correct, this may not be the most
performant solution for very large TINs or complex refinement scenarios.
Future optimizations could focus on more localized updates to the queue.

about nested acceptance: rejection sampler sorts samples based on distance and assumes that the n_samples first samples are the accepted sample. however when several distance functions and and thresholds are used as acceptance criterion, the smallest samples selected based on any one distance measure could contain samples that are not acceptable based on another distance measure and associated threshold.

about what was fixed: previous version checked whether a new batch contains samples where one or more distance measure is not below threshold and substituted all distances in such samples with infinities. this would ensure that the samples would not be sorted as smallest ones when the batch is merged with previous samples. however based on travis, the distances that were overwritten are a read-only variable in linux. hence this new version does not overwrite the distances but checks whether there are acceptable samples in a batch and if so, merges these with the previous samples.
